\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{توقع} (tavaqqo)}{توقع (tavaqqo)}]{\ur{توقع} (tavaqqo) — what one expects (to happen)}

\label{lesson:UR-C543-tavaqqo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a point (in an argument), then the Urdu for a summary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{توقع}}
\textbf{\ur{توقع}} — \emph{tavaqqo} — \textquotedblleft{}what one expects (to happen)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{نتیجہ} \ur{توقع} \ur{سے} \ur{بہتر} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{جشن} \ur{منائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar natījā tavaqqo se behtar huā to jashn manāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the result is better than expected, we'll celebrate.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{توقع}} (\emph{tavaqqo}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tawaqquʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}expecting, waiting for\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tavaqqo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tavaqqo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar natījā tavaqqo se behtar huā to jashn manāeṅ ge.} — If the result is better than expected, we'll celebrate.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a point (in an argument), then the Urdu for a summary, then say \emph{tavaqqo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{توقع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What one expects (to happen)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی} (pesh goī)}{پیش گوئی (pesh goī)}]{\ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی} (pesh goī) — a prediction}

\label{lesson:UR-C543-pesh-goi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a summary, then the Urdu for what one expects.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی}}
\textbf{\ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی}} — \emph{pesh goī} — \textquotedblleft{}a prediction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی} \ur{ٹھیک} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{کل} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar pesh goī ṭhīk hai to kal bārish ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the forecast is right, it will rain tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی}} (\emph{pesh goī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{pēshgōī}, \textquotedblleft{}a prediction\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{pēsh}, \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{gō-}, \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}, with the noun ending \emph{-ī}: saying a thing before it happens.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pesh goī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pesh goī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar pesh goī ṭhīk hai to kal bārish ho gī.} — If the forecast is right, it will rain tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a summary, then the Urdu for what one expects, then say \emph{pesh goī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پیش} \ur{گوئی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A prediction\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تاڑنا} (tāṛnā)}{تاڑنا (tāṛnā)}]{\ur{تاڑنا} (tāṛnā) — to see through (someone's plan); to catch on}

\label{lesson:UR-C543-tarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for what one expects, then the Urdu for a prediction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تاڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تاڑنا}} — \emph{tāṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to see through (someone's plan); to catch on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{امی} \ur{نے} \ur{ہماری} \ur{بات} \ur{تاڑی} \ur{تو} \ur{مشکل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ammī ne hamārī bāt tāṛī to mushkil ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If our mother sees through our plan, there'll be trouble.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سب} \ur{کچھ} \ur{تاڑا}, \emph{us ne sab kuchh tāṛā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تاڑنا}} (\emph{tāṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{tāṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*taḍati}, \textquotedblleft{}stretches\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5633).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāṛnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ammī ne hamārī bāt tāṛī to mushkil ho gī.} — If our mother sees through our plan, there'll be trouble.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for what one expects, then the Urdu for a prediction, then say \emph{tāṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آنکنا} (āṅknā)}{آنکنا (āṅknā)}]{\ur{آنکنا} (āṅknā) — to put a value on; to appraise}

\label{lesson:UR-C543-ankna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a prediction, then the Urdu for to see through.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آنکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{آنکنا}} — \emph{āṅknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to put a value on; to appraise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{سنار} \ur{نے} \ur{انگوٹھی} \ur{آنکی} \ur{تو} \ur{قیمت} \ur{بتائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sunār ne angūṭhī āṅkī to qīmat batāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the goldsmith values the ring, he'll tell us the price.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{زمین} \ur{کی} \ur{قیمت} \ur{آنکی}, \emph{us ne zamīn kī qīmat āṅkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آنکنا}} (\emph{āṅknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ã̄knā}, \textquotedblleft{}to mark, to appraise\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{aṅkayati}, \textquotedblleft{}marks\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 104).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{درست} (durust)}{درست (durust)}]{\ur{درست} (durust) — correct; right}

\label{lesson:UR-C543-durust}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to see through, then the Urdu for to put a value on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{درست}}
\textbf{\ur{درست}} — \emph{durust} — \textquotedblleft{}correct; right\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{جواب} \ur{درست} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{آپ} \ur{جیت} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih javāb durust hai to āp jīt gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{درست}} (\emph{durust}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{durust}, \textquotedblleft{}whole, sound, right\textquotedblright{}.
